Question 1

Load in the DDT data:

# Get DDT Data
ddt <- readxl::read_xls("~/Desktop/OU_Masters/Summer_2026/MATH-4753G_Summer_2026/K25936_Downloads/K25936_Downloads/Excel/DDT.XLS")

Part a

Using the DDT data set make a barplot of SPECIES using ggplot2:

# Make boxplots - need group = 1 so ggplot treats entire data set as 1 group
ddt |> 
    ggplot(aes(x = SPECIES, y = after_stat(prop), group = 1)) +
      geom_bar() +
        labs(title = "Boxplots of Species Proportions",
             subtitle = "Jason M. Klemm")

To do this I piped the DDT data to ggplot and used \(x\) as SPECIES and then \(y\) with after_stat(prop) to get the proportions instead of counts. I also needed to set group = 1 so that the entire data set was treated as a single group - ensured proportion calculation was done correctly. Then I used geom_bar to get the barplots and labs to make the title.

Part b

Using the DDT data create barplots of RIVER for each SPECIES:

# Make barplots for RIVER colored by SPECIES - set position to dodge to get no overlap
ddt |> 
    ggplot(aes(x = RIVER)) +
      geom_bar(aes(fill = SPECIES), position = "dodge") + 
        labs(title = "Count of Species by River",
             subtitle = "Jason M. Klemm")

To do this I piped the DDT data to ggplot and used \(x\) as SPECIES leaving \(y\) to represent counts. Then I used geom_bar to get the barplots with fill = SPECIES to color by species and position = "dodge" so SPECIES barplots didn’t overlap in each river category, and labs to make the title.

Part c

Same plot from part b but with the coordinates flipped:

# Same code as Part b but specify y as RIVER instead of x
ddt |> 
    ggplot(aes(y = RIVER)) +
      geom_bar(aes(fill = SPECIES), position = "dodge") + 
        labs(title = "Count of Species by River",
             subtitle = "Jason M. Klemm")

To do this I did the same process as in Part b but set \(y\) as species in ggplot and let \(x\) represent the counts.

Part d

Create boxplots for the CCATFISH lengths over the RIVERS of the Tennessee river system:

# Make boxplots - filter for CCATFISH and fill for RIVER
ddt |> 
    filter(SPECIES == "CCATFISH") |> 
      ggplot(aes(x = SPECIES, y = LENGTH)) +
        geom_boxplot(aes(fill = RIVER)) +
          labs(title = "Length of Catfish by River",
               subtitle = "Jason M. Klemm")

Here I filtered the DDT data set for only the Catfish species. This was then piped to ggplot with \(x\) as SPECIES and \(y\) as LENGTH. I used geom_boxplot to get the boxplots and let fill = RIVER to color them by River, and used labs to make the title.

Part e

Using dplyr and the necessary verbs create the following tibble from the DDT data set. Where the ddt data frame has two new columns created, log(LENGTH) and log(WEIGHT). The variables in the tibble are meanL (mean LENGTH), meanW (mean WEIGHT), sdlL (standard devialtion of log(LENGTH)) and sdlW (standard deviation of log(WEIGHT)):

# Make new data frame with the calculated log_length and log_weight
ddt_new <- ddt |> mutate(log_length = log(LENGTH), 
                         log_weight = log(WEIGHT))

# Use new data frame to make required tibble with summarise
ddt_new |> 
    group_by(SPECIES) |> 
      summarise(n = n(), 
                meanL = mean(LENGTH), 
                meanW = mean(WEIGHT),
                sdlL = sd(log_length),
                sdlW = sd(log_weight))
## # A tibble: 3 × 6
##   SPECIES       n meanL meanW  sdlL  sdlW
##   <chr>     <int> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
## 1 CCATFISH     96  44.7  987. 0.108 0.284
## 2 LMBASS       12  26.5  629  0.175 0.534
## 3 SMBUFFALO    36  43.1 1356. 0.132 0.383

To make the tibble I made a new DDT data set with log-length and log-weight columns using mutate - used natural log transformation. From there I used the new data set, grouped by species, and then used summarise to get n as species count, meanL as mean length, meanW as mean weight, sdlL as standard deviation of the log-length and sdlW as standard deviation of the log-weight.

Part f

Make a scatterplot:

# Make the scatterplot with fitted curves - filter for TRM river then have point and smooth
ddt |> 
    filter(RIVER == "TRM") |> 
      ggplot(aes(x = LENGTH, y = WEIGHT, color = SPECIES)) +
        geom_point() +
        geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x + I(x**2)) +
          labs(title = "Quadratic Relationship of Weight vs. Length of Fish in the TRM River",
               subtitle = "Jason M. Klemm")

To do this I filtered the DDT data set for the TRM River only. This was then piped to ggplot where \(x\) is LENGTH, \(y\) is WEIGHT and the color set as by species. I used geom_point to get the data points and geom_smooth with the provided method and formula to generate the fitted curves. Then I used labs to make the title.

Question 2

Part a

Count the carriers, sort them and display the last 4 lines:

# Group by carriers - use summarise to get count and then arrange followed by slice_tail
flights |> 
    group_by(carrier) |> 
      summarise(n = n()) |> 
        arrange(desc(n)) |> 
          slice_tail(n = 4) 
## # A tibble: 4 × 2
##   carrier     n
##   <chr>   <int>
## 1 F9        685
## 2 YV        601
## 3 HA        342
## 4 OO         32

To do this I grouped the flights data by carrier and then used summarise to get the counts. I used arrange and specified in descending order using desc, then used slice_tail to get the last four entries.

Part b

Group the flights by origin and summarize by the median departure delay and number in each group:

# Use median for calculation and have na.rm = TRUE to ensure proper calculation - use slice_head for top entries
flights |> 
    group_by(origin) |> 
      summarise(n = n(), delay = median(dep_delay, na.rm = TRUE)) |> 
        slice_head(n = 3)
## # A tibble: 3 × 3
##   origin      n delay
##   <chr>   <int> <dbl>
## 1 EWR    120835    -1
## 2 JFK    111279    -1
## 3 LGA    104662    -3

I grouped by origin and piped this to summarise where n is the count and delay is the median of departure delay (na.rm = TRUE to account for NA and get calculation returned). I then used slice_head to get the first 3 entries.

Part c

Create a barplot of the carriers whose planes depart and arrive early:

# Use logical argument to filter early departures and early arrivals
flights |> 
    filter(dep_delay < 0 & arr_delay < 0) |> 
      ggplot(aes(x = carrier)) +
        geom_bar() +
        labs(title = "Carriers with Early Departures and Arrivals",
             subtitle = "Jason M. Klemm")

I used filter with the logical argument to get early departures and early arrivals. Those fields in the data set where represented as minutes where minutes below \(0\) were early departures and arrivals. I piped this to ggplot with \(x\) as carrier and used geom_bar to get barplots. Then I used labs to make the title.

Part d

Create the data frame where the proportion of flights with short delay at departure is defined by when a flight departure delay is <= 30 min and an arrival long delay is defined as arr_delay >= 180 min:

# Use given conditions to make summary and drop all groups so summarising is done with whole data set together
flights |> 
    group_by(year, month, day) |> 
      summarise(prop_delayed = mean(dep_delay <= 30, na.rm = TRUE), 
                number_long_delay = sum(arr_delay >= 180, na.rm = TRUE),
                .groups = "drop")
## # A tibble: 365 × 5
##     year month   day prop_delayed number_long_delay
##    <int> <int> <int>        <dbl>             <int>
##  1  2013     1     1        0.874                 8
##  2  2013     1     2        0.848                 8
##  3  2013     1     3        0.866                 3
##  4  2013     1     4        0.881                 1
##  5  2013     1     5        0.930                 3
##  6  2013     1     6        0.899                 0
##  7  2013     1     7        0.919                 2
##  8  2013     1     8        0.941                 1
##  9  2013     1     9        0.957                 2
## 10  2013     1    10        0.946                 3
## # ℹ 355 more rows

Here I grouped the flights data by year, month and day. I piped this to summarise where the proportion of delayed was the mean of those having a departure delay less than or equal to 30 minutes. Then the number of flights with a long arrival delay was the sum of those with an arrival delay greater than or equal to 180 minutes. I also used .groups = "drop" so that summarise used no grouping when calculating. Additionally, in summarise I directly used mean and sum to get the correct calculations because the logical expression in each function gives TRUE and FALSE that convert to 1 and 0 as numeric, which is essentially a count that gets collapse and calculated.

Part e

# Use given code to get new flight data frame
flight_new <- flights |> 
    mutate(
      situation = case_when(is.na(arr_delay) ~ "cancelled",
                            arr_delay < -25  ~ "very early",
                            arr_delay < -10  ~ "early",
                            abs(arr_delay) <= 10 ~ "on time",
                            arr_delay < 60       ~ "late",
                            arr_delay < Inf      ~ "very late",),
      .keep = "used") |> 
# Use mutate to reorder factor so the legend is in the correct order
    mutate(situation = fct_relevel(situation, 
                                  "cancelled", 
                                  "very early", 
                                  "early", 
                                  "on time", 
                                  "late", 
                                  "very late"))

# Make the barplots
flight_new |> 
    ggplot(aes(x = situation)) +
      geom_bar(aes(fill = situation)) +
        labs(title = "Situations of Flight Arrivals",
             subtitle = "Jason M. Klemm")

I used the given code from the lab and then used mutate with fct_relevel to get the factors for situation in the correct order for the barplots. The new data set made from the given code with the reordered situation factors was piped to ggplot with \(x\) as situation and \(y\) as count. I used geom_bar to get the barplots and had them fill by situation. Then I used labs to make the title.

Part f

Make a histogram (bins = 40) of the air_time variable for all flights with origin JFK or EWR.

# Filter to origin being JFK or EWR and then make the histogram with 40 bins
flights |> 
    filter(origin == "JFK" | origin == "EWR") |> 
      ggplot(aes(x = air_time, fill = origin)) +
        geom_histogram(bins = 40) +
          labs(title = "Distribution of Flight Air Time",
               subtitle = "Jason M. Klemm")
## Warning: Removed 5908 rows containing non-finite outside the scale range
## (`stat_bin()`).

I used to filter to get origin only as JFK or EWR and then piped this to ggplot. From there I set \(x\) as air time and let \(y\) be count and fill color to be by origin. Then I used geom_histogram with the bins set at \(40\) and labs to make the title.

Question 3

Find all the names that repeat the first three letters at the end of their name in reverse order with one vowel in between the two groups. That is (ABC)(VOWEL)(CBA):

# Make lowercase name column - filter with str_detect and correct pattern then select name column at end
babynames |> 
    mutate(lowers = str_to_lower(name)) |> 
      filter(str_detect(lowers, pattern = "^(.)(.)(.)[aeiou]\\3\\2\\1$")) |> 
        select(name)
## # A tibble: 6 × 1
##   name   
##   <chr>  
## 1 Habibah
## 2 Habibah
## 3 Habibah
## 4 Habibah
## 5 Habibah
## 6 Habibah

Here I make a lowercase name column to help make the regular expression patterning easier. I used filter with str_detect inside it to get the names with pattern I wanted. The pattern is three characters (any) at the start followed by any vowel and then the same three characters at the start in reverse order at the end. I then used select to get the name column of all names that matched this pattern.

Question 4

Find the names of babies that have a sequence of two letters then immediately 2 vowels and end with the same sequence, that is the name contains for example LETTERS(AB)(AE)LETTERS(AB)(AE).

# Use same process as in Question 3 but have new pattern
babynames |> 
    mutate(lowers = str_to_lower(name)) |> 
      filter(str_detect(lowers, pattern = "(..[aeiou]{2}).*\\1$")) |> 
        select(name)
## # A tibble: 1 × 1
##   name      
##   <chr>     
## 1 Arielmarie

Same process as in Question 3 but the pattern was different. The pattern I have here is a group of any two characters followed by any two vowels, then another group of any amount of characters followed by the same first group at the end.
